mechanism_narrative: Persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 4.0%) compresses discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy remains accommodative.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 4.0% (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate vs 50%).

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.5% (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) triggers aggressive monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.5% (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate vs 50%).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST < 1350k) and retail sales (RSAFS < 680k) signal broad consumer demand contraction, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: Joint decline in HOUST < 1350k and RSAFS < 680k fails to predict negative SPX returns: 20-day returns positive in >55% of such periods (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 4.5%) activates Fed easing policy, boosting equity valuations through lower discount rates and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in >55% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5% (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate vs 50%).

mechanism_narrative: Strong non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS > 155k) indicates robust labor market conditions, increasing consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in >55% of periods when PAYEMS > 155k (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate vs 50%).

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate profits and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in >55% of periods when INDPRO < 100 (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate vs 50%).

mechanism_narrative: Real GDP growth below 0.5% annualized (GDPC1 < 0.5%) indicates late-cycle economic slowdown, reducing corporate earnings growth and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in >55% of periods when GDPC1 < 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate vs 50%).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent federal funds rate hikes (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) signal aggressive monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Joint condition FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.5% fails to predict negative SPX returns: 20-day returns positive in >55% of such periods (p-value > 0.05).
